newsitem.title: GERMANY: German markets watchdog to probe Traub.
newsitem.headline: German markets watchdog to probe Traub.

text.p: Germany's stock market watchdog, the BAWe, said on Thursday evening it had started an investigation into machine tool maker Traub AG following its announcement this week of plans to file for bankruptcy.

Traub on Tuesday released its plans in the form of a regular faxed press statement, rather than an electronic so-called "ad-hoc" transmission which German law requires for potentially market-moving information.
A spokesman for the BAWe confirmed a report to appear in Friday's Die Welt newspaper that it had started a probe into Traub.
The spokesman said the BAWe would now assess whether the content of Traub's statement warranted ad-hoc electronic delivery and whether the company might have violated insider trading rules.
In its statement, Traub, which declared itself insolvent in October, said its efforts to scale back debt with its creditors had failed and it therefore needed to file for bankruptcy.
